report:
Antecedentes Clínicos:
Gonalgia derecha.
Hallazgos:
Adelgazamiento impresiona secuelar del LCA. Correlacionar con clínica.
LCP y ligamento colateral lateral sin alteraciones. Leve engrosamiento impresiona secuelar del componente
superficial del ligamento colateral medial. El resto de los componentes del complejo medial sin alteraciones.
Aumento de señal de la unión meniscocapsular del cuerno posterior del menisco medial que podría
representar una lesión parcial regional.
Rotura compleja de la unión del cuerno posterior con la raíz meniscal posterior del menisco lateral, sin
significativo desplazamiento de segmentos.
Úlcera condral de espesor total del aspecto posterior de la zona de carga del cóndilo femoral lateral de 8 x 5
mm en sus ejes anteroposterior y mediolateral respectivamente con cambios óseos secundarios. Úlceras
condrales focales de espesor total con cambios óseos secundarios al aspecto posterior del platillo tibial
lateral asociado a edema óseo fractura subcortical regional.
No hay significativo derrame articular ni quistes poplíteos.
Tendones cuadricipital, la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de límites normales. Leve
aumento de señal del tercio proximal del tendón rotuliano, sin signos de rotura.
Impresión:
Adelgazamiento que impresiona secuelar del LCA, correlacionar con clínica. Edema óseo asociado pequeña
fractura subcortical del aspecto posterior de platillo tibial lateral que podría representar evento de
inestabilidad.
Rotura compleja de la unión del cuerno posterior con la raíz meniscal posterior del menisco lateral.
Aumento de señal del meniscocapsular del cuerno posterior del menisco medial que podría representar una
lesión parcial regional.
Condropatía con lesiones grado 4 del aspecto posterior de la zona de carga del compartimento femorotibial
lateral

MRI of left Knee with 
-3-Plane Loc, Sag T2 FS, Sag PD FS, Sag T1, Cor T2 FS, Ax T2 FS, Apparent Diffusion Coefficient (mm2/s), Ax DWI B800


* Osteochondral defect of centroinfterior portion of medial femoral condyle with partially detached osteochondral fragment with fluid interface in the unstable osteochondral fragment (srs: [ID]. 
> Subchondral edema in medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau; wearing of articular cartilage and spur formation of left knee; tiny subchondral cyst in medial femoral condyle.
> Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar, lateral and medial plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.
> The contour of ACL is not in a straight line and increase signal intensity inside and buckling of posterior cruciate ligament and anterior tibial translation , in favor of complete tear of ACL.
> There are linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, it extends into the surface, in favor of tear.
> Lateral meniscus appears to be normal.
> Both medial & lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
> A lobulated cystic lesion in medial popliteal fossa between the tendons of the medial head of the gastrocnemius and the semimembranosus muscles, in favor of Baker's cyst, about 5 cm in length; perifocal edema surround the cystic lesion.
    Increased fat stranding along pes  pes anserinus, in favor of mild anserine bursitis.
> Subcutaneous infiltration over prepatellar to infrapatellar region.

Impression: 
1. C/W stage 3 osteonecrosis of left medial femoral conylde and osteoarthritis of left knee.
2. ACL tear.
3. Tear of posterior horn of medial meniscus.
4. Synovitis of left knee with suprapatellar bursitis and Baker's cyst.
5. R/O mild anserine bursitis.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Pain.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.16 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
There is intense bone marrow edema within the medial femoral condyle with a subchondral crescent of low signal at the central weightbearing aspect, consistent with a subchondral insufficiency fracture. There is no significant articular surface collapse. No evidence of osteonecrosis. Mild degenerative subchondral cystic change is present at the inferior patella. Background bone marrow signal is otherwise normal. 

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Small, ruptured Baker cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: There is a large radial tear at the posterior root attachment. Moderate extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: Mild to moderate cartilage thinning/fissuring diffusely.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: There is fraying of the inner margin along the body and posterior horn. Small tear at the posterior root attachment.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Cartilage appears intact.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: There is moderate to severe cartilage loss at the patella and trochlea, with mild subchondral cystic change.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Intact, with surrounding edema compatible with hyperemia related to adjacent medial compartment disease.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 8 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Diffuse periarticular soft tissue edema, most prominent medially.

IMPRESSION:

1. Subchondral insufficiency fracture at the weightbearing aspect of the medial femoral condyle.
2. Tear at the posterior root attachment of the medial meniscus with moderate extrusion. Small tear of the lateral meniscus.
3. Chondrosis in the patellofemoral and medial tibiofemoral compartment.
4. Small, ruptured Baker cyst.

MRI of left  Knee with 
-3-Plane Loc, Sag T2 FS, Sag T1, Cor T2 FS, Ax T2 FS, AX GRE T2*, Cor T2 FS, Screen Save

> Status of hemophilia B according to history
> Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with intermediate to mild hypointensity signal  on T1WI and heterogenous hyperintenisty signal inside, but no significant fluid-fluid interface,  C/W chronic hemarthrosis; suprapatellar and medial plicae.
    Irregular hypointensity signal material surround the joint capsule in left joint on all sequence, in favor of hypertrophy of the synovium with hemosiderin deposition ( especially at intercondylar region),  reflecting of hemophilic synovitis.
> Wearing of articular cartilage of left knee and mild mild subchondral bone edema and cysts over distal femur and tibial plateua; in favorof some  bone erosions.
> Suspicious of linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, with suspicious of extending into the surface, R/O tear. 
> A lobulated cystic lesion in medial popliteal fossa between the tendons of the medial head of the gastrocnemius and the semimembranosus muscles, in favor of Baker's cyst, about 5 cm in length; [DATE] . Mild perifocal edema.
> Mild  subcutaneous edema over right knee and muscle edema over vastus medialis muscle.
> Subcutanoues edema and interstitial muscle edema over right proximal leg, more prominent in comparison with last MRI.
> Interstitial increased signal intensity of the muscles in left lower thigh, major at  anterior and posteror compartment of left lower thigh, including quadriceps muscles and biceps femoris muscle; in favor of intermusuclar hyperintensity area along biceps femoris muscle, maybe due to intermuscular edema/ hemorrhage .
    Minimal fluid accumulation in semimembranousus muscle and semitendinousus tendon
    
Impression: 
1. C/W hemophilic arthropathy of  left knee joint with prominent hemophilic synovitis and in favor of  chronic hemarthrosis and bulging of suprapatellar bursitis and Baker's cyst; patellar plicae.
2. [DATE]; in favor of some intermuscular edema/ hemorrahge along biceps femoris muscle.
3. R/O degeneration and tear of posterior horn of medial meniscus.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation and further management

Interprétation :

Minime épanchement intra-articulaire d’allure physiologique. Liséré de liquide au sein du récessus poplité sans kyste de Baker significatif.

Les ménisques interne et externe sont intacts sans déchirure. Le ménisque externe est légèrement discoïde.

Le ligament collatéral interne, le complexe ligamentaire collatéral externe, les ligaments croisés antérieur et postérieur sont intacts sans déchirure. Légère infiltration kystique ganglionnaire au sein du ligament croisé antérieur distal et en intra-osseux sous son insertion distale.

Légère atténuation des surfaces chondrales au compartiment fémoro-tibial interne et aspect légèrement hétérogène avec fissure chondrale superficielle le long du compartiment fémoro-tibial externe en lien avec une légère chondropathie. Foyer de chondropathie focale sévère le long de la surface portante du condyle fémoral interne avec fissure chondrale transfixiante et changements sous-chondraux réactionnels.

L’alignement patellofémoral est préservé. Les tendons du quadriceps distal et patellaire sont intacts sans déchirure. Légère tendinose du tendon patellaire proximal. Légère chondropathie diffuse au compartiment patellofémoral avec fibrillation chondrale superficielle et fissures plus marquées, partielle, le long de la facette patellaire externe et transfixiante le long de la facette patellaire interne avec début de changements sous-chondraux réactionnels, en lien avec des foyers de chondropathie respectivement modéré sévère.

Conclusion :

Il n’y a pas de dérangement interne (pas de déchirure méniscale ou ligamentaire significative). 

Pas d’épanchement intra-articulaire significatif. 

Légère chondropathie tricompartimentale avec foyer de chondropathie focale sévère le long de la surface portante du condyle fémoral interne et le long de la facette patellaire interne.

In the medial compartment, the meniscus is not torn and there is no focal chondrosis or chondral injury. 
 The lateral compartment, the meniscus is not torn and there is no focal chondrosis or chondral injury. 
 The patellofemoral joint, the patellar and trochlear cartilage appears congruent without chondral lesion. The medial patellofemoral ligament is intact.  
 In the intercondylar notch, the anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments are intact. There is no tibial translation. 
 The medial collateral ligament complexes are intact. The posteromedial oblique ligament is intact.  
 The lateral collateral ligament complexes are intact. The popliteofibular ligament is intact. The meniscopopliteal fascicles are intact.  
 The extensor mechanism is normal.  
 No knee effusion is present. The surrounding musculature is normal. There is no fracture or bone contusion. Normal MR examination of the right knee.  Specifically, there is no evidence of meniscal, ligamentous, or articular cartilage abnormality.

Regelrechtes Knochenmarksignal. Oberflächliche Irregularitäten des Knorpel femoral. Kein tiefgreifender oder vollschichtiger Knorpeldefekt. Kein subchondrales Ödem. Radiärer Riss am Übergang von der Pars intermedia zum Hinterhorn des Innenmeniskus (Serie 3/ Image 98). Intaktes MCL.

Laterales Kompartiment:
Regelrechtes Knochenmarksignal. Oberflächliche Irregularitäten des Knorpel femoral. Kein tiefgreifender oder vollschichtiger Knorpeldefekt. Kein subchondrales Ödem. Intakter Außenmeniskus. Kleine parameniskale Zysten angrenzend an die Pars intermedia des Außenmeniskus (Serie 5/ Image 21). Intaktes LCL.

Femoropatellares Gleitlager und Trochlea:
Regelrechtes Knochenmarksignal. Intakter Knorpel. Regelrechte Darstellung der Quadrizeps- und der Patellarsehne.

Kreuzbänder:
